extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for journalists on inclusive, accurate and respectful terminology and usage when reporting about people, communities, religions, illnesses, identities and related topics. Entries explain preferred terms, capitalization, usage cautions, and when to avoid or attribute outdated/offensive language.

rubrics_metrics.name: LGBTQ+
rubrics_metrics.description: The Diversity Style Guide recommends the more inclusive term LGBTQ+.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stylebook notes: referring to the 'LGBTQ+ community' is tempting but inaccurate because it is a broad and sometimes loosely bound group; 'LGBTQ+ people' is usually more accurate. Do not refer to an individual as LGBTQ or LGBTQ+. (Updated March 2023.)

rubrics_metrics.name: lifestyle
rubrics_metrics.description: An inaccurate term sometimes used to describe the lives of gay, lesbian, bisexual and transgender people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sexual orientation may be part of a broader lifestyle but is not one in itself; avoid using 'lifestyle' to describe sexual orientation. See sexual orientation, sexual preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: linguistic racism
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrimination based on accent, dialect or speech patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts can be overt (mocking someone's speech) or covert (saying someone is unintelligible because of an accent, complimenting 'speaks English well' when born speaking that language). Certain languages/dialects are undervalued; Spanish, Asian languages and AAVE may be especially targeted. Common examples include questions like 'Where are you from?' and 'You don’t sound Black.' (Added June 2021.)

rubrics_metrics.name: little person
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry pointer for terminology regarding short-statured people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See dwarf, midget, short stature for preferred and avoidable terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: liturgy
rubrics_metrics.description: Term with different uses for Western and Eastern Christians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Among Roman Catholics and Protestants, lowercase 'liturgy' refers to a standard set of prayers and practices; it can also mean the service of worship. For Orthodox Christians and Eastern Catholics, use uppercase 'Liturgy' and avoid the lowercase use with their churches. Nonliturgical churches (e.g., most Baptist, Pentecostal) vary their services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lord (capitalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Always capitalize when referring to God in a monotheistic faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as in 'Lord Jesus' or 'Lord Krishna.'

rubrics_metrics.name: lover
rubrics_metrics.description: Term some individuals prefer for a sexual partner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatives include girlfriend, boyfriend and partner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lubavitch, Lubavitcher
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred naming and background on the Hasidic movement (also called Chabad-Lubavitch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides historical background and notes common internal usages (e.g., 'The Rebbe'). See Chabad.

rubrics_metrics.name: lupus
rubrics_metrics.description: Chronic autoimmune disease that can affect many organs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains symptoms and notes lupus most often affects black women.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lutheran
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on referring to members of a Protestant denomination tracing roots to Martin Luther.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On first reference use the Rev. and the cleric’s full name; on second reference use only the cleric’s last name. Explains major bodies (ELCA, Missouri Synod) and typical congregational governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: madman
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated pejorative term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See crazy/crazed, psycho, nuts, lunatic, deranged, wacko (avoid).

rubrics_metrics.name: madrassa
rubrics_metrics.description: A Muslim place of learning usually associated with a mosque.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as definition; be aware of context when reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mahatma
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanskrit honorific meaning 'great soul', associated with M.K. Gandhi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide definition and cultural context.

rubrics_metrics.name: mainline Protestant
rubrics_metrics.description: Designation for a group of moderate-to-liberal Protestant churches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists common denominations included and explains the term's usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Malaysian names
rubrics_metrics.description: Naming conventions and special considerations for Malaysians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some Malaysians do not use family names and use honorifics; Malaysian Chinese and Malaysian Muslims follow special naming rules—be careful with second references.

rubrics_metrics.name: male-to-female (MtF), female-to-male (FtM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outdated ways to describe trans people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid these terms unless quoting a trans source; use 'trans woman' and 'trans man' instead. (Updated February 2021.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandarin
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes important differences from Cantonese and usage guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandarin is the spoken language of China and Taiwan; one 'speaks Mandarin' but 'writes Chinese.' Cantonese and other regional varieties are different; be precise when identifying dialects versus the written language.

rubrics_metrics.name: manga
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of comic developed in Japan with stylistic features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains stylistic evolution and audience; include content warnings if adult content is involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: manong / manang
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms of respect for older Filipino men/women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pronunciation and usage: 'manong' precedes the first name of older Filipino men; 'manang' for older Filipina women.

rubrics_metrics.name: mantra
rubrics_metrics.description: Syllable, word or phrase with spiritual power used in meditation/ritual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common among Hindus, Buddhists and Jains; traditionally drawn from Sanskrit scriptures; examples and cultural context provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: marriage (same-sex reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred terminology when reporting on marriage for same-sex couples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'marriage equality' or 'marriage for same-sex couples'; avoid 'gay marriage' and 'same-sex marriage' as they can suggest difference. Notes Obergefell v. Hodges (2015) guaranteeing right to marry.

rubrics_metrics.name: martial arts
rubrics_metrics.description: Armed and unarmed fighting sports or skills, mainly East Asian origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes types and influences; cautions that martial-arts imagery can be abused (e.g., editorial cartoons) and cross-references Asia stereotypes guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: masjid
rubrics_metrics.description: Urdu word for mosque; place of prayer and meeting for Muslims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition and brief context (e.g., Babri Masjid controversy).

rubrics_metrics.name: mass (worship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Term used by Latin Catholics and some high-church Anglicans for a worship service that includes Holy Communion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize 'Mass' when referring to Roman Catholic celebration of worship; 'funeral Mass' lowercases preceding adjectives. For Catholics, 'Mass is celebrated' (AP accepts 'celebrated' only). Orthodox Christians call their service the Divine Liturgy and usage differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: mass incarceration
rubrics_metrics.description: Increased rates of imprisonment resulting from tougher penalties, especially for drug offenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains racial disparities, sentencing differences, growth in female incarceration and references NAACP/Southern Coalition/Sentencing Commission data and related reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: master bedroom/bathroom
rubrics_metrics.description: Terminology for principal rooms in a home with problematic connotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'master bedroom'/'master bathroom' because of racist and sexist undertones; use 'owner’s suite' or 'primary bedroom' instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: McCarran-Walter Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Immigration and Nationality Act of 1952; limited Asian immigration quotas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides historical context and impact; use full name on first mention.

rubrics_metrics.name: mehndi
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional Indian/diapsora henna body art used in ceremonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain cultural roots and growing popularity; avoid exoticizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: MENA (Middle Eastern or North African)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviation for Middle East and North Africa region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Middle Eastern or North African descent' on first reference; if using 'MENA' explain it.

rubrics_metrics.name: mental health
rubrics_metrics.description: State of well-being enabling coping, productivity, and realization of potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge cultural differences and varying professional definitions; use people-first language and be cautious when labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: mental health professional
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of different professionals who treat mental health challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish psychiatrist, psychoanalyst, psychologist, psychotherapist, social worker, marriage and family therapist, etc. Ask the professional how they should be identified and avoid 'shrink' except in quotes. HIPAA may limit information they can share.

rubrics_metrics.name: mental illness / mental health disorder
rubrics_metrics.description: Health conditions that change thinking, feelings or behavior and cause distress or difficulty functioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use people-first language (e.g., 'person with bipolar disorder' vs 'he is bipolar'); specify diagnosis when possible; refer to diagnosis only when relevant and sourced. Follow APA guidance and indicate when diagnosis is unconfirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: mentally retarded / mentally disabled terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms formerly used that are now outdated and offensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'mentally retarded' / 'retard'; use 'intellectual disability' or 'developmental disability' and people-first language. Outdated terms may be used only in historical context with attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: messiah / Messiah
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization guidance depending on religious vs secular use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize in religious uses (Christian reference to Jesus), lowercase in secular contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodist Episcopal Church
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical description of the denomination and its role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use full historical name when relevant; provides background and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mexican / Mexican-American
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage distinction between nationality and ancestry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Mexican' for anyone of Mexican citizenship; use 'Mexican American' for those of Mexican ancestry who are U.S. permanent residents or citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: microaggressions / racial microaggressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Slights and snubs based on racial discrimination, sometimes unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include examples (e.g., 'You don’t act like a normal Black person'); note accumulating effects on mental health and performance and reference further reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Middle East
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic/region definition centered on Western Asia, Southeastern Europe and North Africa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP-adopted definition: southwest Asia west of Pakistan/Afghanistan (lists countries) and northeastern Africa (Egypt, Sudan). 'Middle East' preferred; 'Mideast' acceptable. Adjective: Middle-Eastern; noun: Middle-Easterner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Middle Passage
rubrics_metrics.description: The transatlantic voyages between Africa and the Americas that carried enslaved Africans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide historical context and link to slavery entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: midget
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated/derogatory term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See dwarf, little person, short stature; avoid using 'midget.'

rubrics_metrics.name: midlife
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred term for people in middle age; more inclusive than 'boomers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Midlife typically spans early 40s to early 60s; use with caution and precision where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: militant
rubrics_metrics.description: Term describing aggressive activists or someone engaged in warfare; neutral but often misused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'militant' in place of 'terrorist.' Avoid describing a Black person as 'militant' simply for being hostile/controversial. 'Militant' is neutral; 'terrorist' implies reprehensible behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Million Man March / Million Woman March
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical descriptions of large rallies (1995, 1997).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include event dates, organizers, purposes and reported attendance; treat names and claims carefully (organizers vs estimates).

rubrics_metrics.name: minister
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage and capitalization for clergy across denominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most Protestant denominations use 'minister' (not a formal title—lowercase). For Nation of Islam it is a title and should be capitalized before a name. In Catholicism, distinguish ordained ministers (priests, deacons) and lay ministers.

rubrics_metrics.name: minority, racial minority
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms historically referring to non-White racial groups but problematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid referring to an individual as 'a minority.' Prefer how people self-identify; use 'people of color' when appropriate. The term 'minority' may be needed in specific data contexts (e.g., 'minority-owned businesses').

rubrics_metrics.name: misgender
rubrics_metrics.description: Act of referring to someone by the wrong gender (pronouns or gendered words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some newsrooms avoid pronouns and gender-specific words in breaking news when gender can't be confirmed; be careful and confirm gender identity when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: mixed-status couple / mixed-status family
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to families or couples with differing immigration status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also may be used by health workers to describe serodiscordant sexual relationships (HIV-positive/negative); clarify intended meaning in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: mixed / mixed-race
rubrics_metrics.description: See biracial, multiracial and related terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use preferred terminology and be precise about self-identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: model minority
rubrics_metrics.description: Belief that a particular group achieves greater success than population average (often applied to Asians).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note concerns: implies group advantage and masks discrimination and socioeconomic diversity; avoid uncritical use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modern Orthodox
rubrics_metrics.description: Movement within Orthodox Judaism integrating tradition with secular life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term accepted among Jews but encompasses a spectrum; clarify with subjects where they see themselves if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mongolian names
rubrics_metrics.description: Complex naming rules involving patronymics, matronymics and clan names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware second-reference usage; verify correct naming conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mongoloid
rubrics_metrics.description: Historic, offensive term once used to refer to people with Down syndrome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered highly derogatory; always avoid using 'Mongoloid' to describe someone with Down syndrome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Montgomery bus boycott
rubrics_metrics.description: Yearlong 1955–56 protest that galvanized the civil-rights movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include historical outcome (1956 Supreme Court decision declaring segregated seating on buses unconstitutional) and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moonie
rubrics_metrics.description: Derogatory term for a member of the Unification Church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use except in direct quotes; see Unification Church for preferred usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mormon Church
rubrics_metrics.description: See Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer the formal name of the church when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moslem
rubrics_metrics.description: Outdated term for Muslims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'Moslem' unless part of a proper name or historical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motown
rubrics_metrics.description: Formerly black-owned record company and musical style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as noun or adjective to describe the musical style or origin city (Detroit).

rubrics_metrics.name: MSM
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviation for 'men who have sex with men.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in behavioral and public health contexts; does not reference sexual identity and is not synonymous with gay and bisexual men. See 'down low.'

rubrics_metrics.name: mulatto
rubrics_metrics.description: Term referring to a person with a white parent and a black parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the term; considered insensitive. Prefer 'biracial.'

rubrics_metrics.name: mullah
rubrics_metrics.description: Shiite term for lower-level clergy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize the title when it precedes a name.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiple personality disorder
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated diagnostic term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See dissociative identity disorder for current terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiple sclerosis (MS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disease of the central nervous system with varied symptoms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe someone as 'someone with multiple sclerosis' and explain manifestations if relevant; avoid 'suffers from' or 'is afflicted with.' 'MS' is acceptable on second reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mumbai
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred current name for the city formerly known as Bombay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Mumbai' and be aware of historical renaming in post-colonial contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: murti
rubrics_metrics.description: In Hinduism, an image or icon of God used during worship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the word 'idol' as a synonym.

rubrics_metrics.name: muscular dystrophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Any of more than 30 genetic diseases causing progressive muscle weakness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe someone as 'someone with muscular dystrophy' and explain specifics; avoid 'suffers from' or 'is afflicted with.' 'MD' acceptable on second reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Muslim American
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage guidance for the compound term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not hyphenate ('Muslim American'); hyphenate when used as a compound modifier (e.g., 'Muslim-American community').

rubrics_metrics.name: Muslim / Muslims
rubrics_metrics.description: Noun/adjective distinction for followers of Islam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Muslim' is a noun (a follower of Muhammad and Islam); use 'Islamic' when referring to the faith or the Islamic world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mx.
rubrics_metrics.description: Gender-neutral courtesy title pronounced 'mix.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred by some transgender or nonbinary people; usage is increasing but still uncommon—newsrooms should respect preference when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Myanmar
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred modern name for the country formerly known as Burma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pronunciation guidance (MEE-YAHN-mar) and cross-reference to 'Burma'.

rubrics_metrics.name: NAACP
rubrics_metrics.description: National Association for the Advancement of Colored People; historical founding info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acronym acceptable in all references; includes note on NAACP Legal Defense and Educational Fund as separate organization—use 'Legal Defense Fund' on second reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: nation (federally recognized tribes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federally recognized tribes are considered self-governing or sovereign nations by Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'nation' when referring to tribal sovereignty; cross-reference American Indian, Native American, tribe entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nation of Islam
rubrics_metrics.description: Religious and political organization formed in 1930 with distinct tenets from traditional Islam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to followers as 'members of the Nation of Islam.' Avoid 'Black Muslim' (derogatory). Nation of Islam clergymen use the title 'minister' which should be capitalized before a name on first reference; use last name on second reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Negro League
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional baseball league for blacks founded in 1920.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide historical context regarding segregation and later integration of Major League Baseball.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native American / Native
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the terms Native American and American Indian and usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both terms generally acceptable; journalists should identify people by their preferred tribal affiliation when reporting on individuals. 'Native' can be an adjective (e.g., Native fashion) but use cautiously. Federal recognition and tribal enrollment rules affect who is considered American Indian. Note 2016 federal change replacing 'American Indian' with 'Native American' in some laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native Hawaiian
rubrics_metrics.description: People tracing lineage and language to Polynesians, known as Kanaka Maoli.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide cultural context and note federal recognition of Native Hawaiians and Pacific Islanders as distinct groups in Census counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander (Census)
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. Census Bureau definition for people with origins in original peoples of Hawaii, Guam, Samoa or other Pacific Islands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that racial categories on the census reflect social definitions recognized in the U.S., not biological or anthropological definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander (umbrella term)
rubrics_metrics.description: Umbrella term used by the Census and other agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes people tracing roots to original peoples of Hawaii, Guam, Samoa or other Pacific Islands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negro
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical term for people of African descent; now generally unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'African American' or 'black.' Do not use 'Negro' to describe a person; acceptable in organization names and historical references (e.g., National Council of Negro Women).

rubrics_metrics.name: Negro Codes
rubrics_metrics.description: See Black codes (historical legal restrictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference for historical reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negro National Anthem
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to the 1899 poem 'Lift Ev’ry Voice and Sing' adopted by the NAACP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context, history and attribution; media can link to performances or recordings when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: neo-paganism
rubrics_metrics.description: Contemporary paganism as distinct from ancient paganism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some groups prefer 'pagan' or 'neo-pagan' depending on whether they emphasize ancient roots or blending old and new practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nepali / Nepalese
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage guidance for people from Nepal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Nepali' is favored in current usage and can be noun or adjective; U.S. press may use 'Nepalese' for those in the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: neuroatypical / neurodivergent
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms describing people with atypical developmental, intellectual or cognitive abilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to refer to people with autism or other developmental differences; contrast with 'neurotypical' for those not on the autism spectrum.
